title: BERNARD VILLEMOT (1911-1989). BALLY. 1989.
description: BERNARD VILLEMOT (1911-1989). BALLY. 1989. 66x44 inches, 167x113 cm. A. Karcher, Paris. Condition A-: minor abrasions at edges; light rippling in image; slightly faded in image. Framed. Bernard Villemot became one of the most recognizable poster designers of his generation, with a style that emulates cartoons and exudes humor and cheerfulness. In the early 1930s, he studied with Paul Colin, and Villemot's work from this time reflects a more curvilinear, Art Deco approach than his later work. In 1949, his early works were exhibited in Paris with those of Raymond Savignac, with whom Villemot is most closely associated. Over the next few decades, he was prolific in his advertising designs for companies like Bally, Perrier, Air France and Orangina. Here, in his last poster, he displays his mastery of the art form. In an impressive vertical format, this lithe lady kicks around the globe, yet her shadow is cast as a man's leg. An alluring and daring poster. Villemot / Bon Salle 313, The Poster 731, Encyclopedie de l'Affiche p. 113.

title: BALLY
description:
PIERRE GAUCHAT (1902-1956)
BALLY. 1935.
50 1/4x36 1/4 inches, 127 1/2x92 cm. Wolfsburg, Zurich.
Condition B+ / A-: small repaired tears and replaced losses in margins. Swiss Graphic artist Pierre Gauchat studied under Otto Baumberger and Ernst Zeller, and later opened his own graphic design workshop. This, considered his most famous poster, exemplifies Lucian Bernhard's tradition of Sachplakate - employing one object and one word to advertise a product - although here, Gauchat places the stylish shoe on a detailed carpet. (It is interesting to note that Gauchat also designed carpets). In 1948, Gauchat won the Swiss National Bank's competition to redesign the country's banknotes, illustrating 1000, 500, 100 and 50 franc notes. Rare. We could find no previous examples at auction. With ink stamps from the Kunsthaus Zürich in the bottom right corner. Modern Poster 190, Avant Garde p. 172, Magic of Things 9, MoMA 312.1937.

description: ROGER EXCOFFON (1910-1983). BALLY. 1964. 46½x62½ inches, 118x158¾ cm. Lavasselais, Paris. Condition B: small drip stains along left image; repaired tears at edges, some into image; creases and restoration at edges and image. Excoffon was a renowned French typographer whose Chambord, Antique Olive and Mistral typefaces are recognized throughout the world. He also ran an advertising agency through which he represented Air France and Perrier, amongst others prominent clients. For his posters, he often employed brushstroke-like flourishes, or sweeps of ink, to help evoke the subject.
